description:
Make the standard failure-probe coverage test publish its derived per-arm census on successful runs, so the conformance result is inspectable even when no assertion fails.

## Background

The coverage guard already derives every machine-readable command arm, executes each registered probe, and builds a diagnostic row naming the observed envelope and code or the declared exemption and reason. Today those rows exist only inside a failing assertion message. A passing standard test therefore leaves no report, despite the parent story requiring the check to report the per-arm result. The report remains test-derived and machine-readable; it must not become another committed arm table.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A passing standard test invocation writes a machine-readable conformance report under the build output directory.
- [hard] REQ-02: The report contains exactly one row for every reflected machine-readable command arm and no stale row.
- [hard] REQ-03: A probed row states whether a canonical envelope rendered, the observed registered error code, and the observed exit status.
- [hard] REQ-04: An exempt row states the exemption and its non-empty recorded reason.
- [hard] REQ-05: The report is derived from the reflected command definitions and canonical failure registry at test time rather than maintained as a committed arm table.
- [hard] REQ-06: Focused tests verify the successful report artifact and retain the existing actionable failure diagnostics.
title: Publish the per-arm conformance census
